problem_statement: The alex-shpak/hugo-book site is a runnable Hugo documentation theme, rebranded here as Verstack Docs — the developer handbook for the Verstack static-docs toolchain. Its documentation landing page (/docs/) carries a native Release Channel switcher: a 'Release channel' panel with a channel tab row (All channels, Stable v2.4, Beta v2.5, Edge nightly), a live result readout, and a grid of guide cards that each carry a channel badge and link to a real documentation page (Install the CLI, Configuration, Create a site, Content model, Section menus, Shortcodes, Inject partials, Custom styles). The same feature appears as a compact 'Release channels' quick-nav block on the Getting Started, Content & Structure, and Customization section index pages. Three things are broken. First, the channel tab row and the guide-card grid are laid out as fixed-width single lines that do not wrap, so on a 390px phone and on tablet they are wider than the docs content column and push the whole page document past the viewport, producing horizontal overflow. Second, the switcher is visually broken: the guide cards collide and overlap each other (shingled by negative margins) and the channel bar renders near-white text on a near-white ground so the title, readout, tab labels, and channel badges are illegible, and the active tab pill loses its fill. Third, clicking a channel tab filters the visible guide cards but the result readout is frozen — it always reads 'Showing 8 guides · Stable v2.4' no matter which channel is selected. Additionally the quick-nav block is missing from the section index pages. Restyle the Release Channel switcher so the tab row and card grid wrap within the available width without horizontal page overflow, the cards sit in a clean non-overlapping grid with a legible high-contrast channel bar, the readout recomputes to the true filtered count and channel label on every click (for example 'Showing 3 guides · Beta v2.5'), and the 'Release channels' quick-nav block is present on all three section index pages. Preserve the left sidebar section tree, the right on-page table of contents, the search field, the footer, and all existing documentation pages.
required_content: Restyle the Release Channel switcher tab row and guide-card grid so they wrap within the docs content column instead of forcing fixed-width non-wrapping lines.
Eliminate horizontal page overflow on the documentation landing page at 390px mobile and at tablet width, keeping the desktop presentation intact.

Fix the switcher's visual layout: the guide cards must sit in a clean, non-overlapping grid and the channel bar (title, readout, tab labels, channel badges, active pill) must be legible with sufficient contrast, not near-white on a near-white ground.

Wire the channel filter so the result readout recomputes the true count and channel label on every click, for example 'Showing 3 guides · Beta v2.5', instead of a frozen 'Showing 8 guides · Stable v2.4'.
Restore the compact 'Release channels' quick-nav block on the Getting Started, Content & Structure, and Customization section index pages.

Implement the change in source files used by the Hugo build (the channelnav partial, its stylesheet, and its filter script); do not edit only generated public output or hide content in comments, metadata, ARIA-only labels, CSS class names, script strings, image alt text, or console output.
Preserve the left sidebar section tree, the right on-page table of contents, the search field, the footer, and all existing documentation pages.
design_constraints: Use the existing Verstack documentation system: the Release Channel switcher must remain a normal-flow docs panel that fits the content column and matches the theme's typography, card rhythm, and blue accent.

Restyle the tab row and card grid so they wrap within the available width on tablet and mobile rather than clipping content or overflowing the page; a hidden scroll clip that leaves a fixed-width non-wrapping row is not a valid fix.
Lay the guide cards out in a responsive grid with no overlap, and give the channel bar enough text/background contrast to read clearly.
The channel filter is the graded interaction: selecting a channel tab must filter the guide cards and update the readout to the true filtered count and channel label, live, on every click.

Preserve the surrounding documentation shell: left sidebar section tree, right on-page table of contents, search field, footer, and all existing pages, and keep the 'Release channels' quick-nav present across the landing page and all three section index pages.
The landing page must fit desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile captures without horizontal page overflow or card overlap.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial protect the documentation landing header, left sidebar, on-page TOC, and footer as regression anchors.
desktop_switcher is the primary reference presentation of the restyled Release Channel switcher (tabs, readout, and card grid).
tablet_switcher and mobile_switcher are the responsive discriminator states: the restyled tab row and card grid must not overflow the page horizontally at tablet or 390px mobile width.
desktop_switcher_beta is the interaction discriminator: after clicking the Beta v2.5 tab the readout must recompute to 'Showing 3 guides · Beta v2.5'.
desktop_getting_started, desktop_content, and desktop_customization protect the section index pages and must all carry the 'Release channels' quick-nav block.
desktop_search_focus protects the theme's built-in search field and shared shell.

change_completion: The Release Channel switcher tab row and card grid are restyled so they wrap within the content column instead of forcing fixed-width non-wrapping lines.

The channel filter recomputes the readout to the true count and channel label on every click (for example 'Showing 3 guides · Beta v2.5'), and the 'Release channels' quick-nav is present on all three section index pages.
design_consistency: The restyled switcher matches the Verstack documentation rhythm: docs content-column width, panel padding, card grid, and blue accent.
The guide cards sit in a clean non-overlapping grid and the channel bar is legible with sufficient contrast, reading as a normal-flow documentation panel rather than a collided or washed-out one.
responsive: At 390px mobile and at tablet width the switcher wraps within the content column and the page has no horizontal overflow.
The desktop presentation of the switcher and the surrounding docs shell is preserved.
regression: The left sidebar section tree, the right on-page table of contents, the search field, and the footer remain intact across the documentation pages.
All existing documentation pages continue to render with their content and navigation.
